what: 6 mm Cast acrylic, tinted through in the speaker's colour, 4 x 8 ft sheet

a laser shop (a CO2 laser, 100 W or more) Laser work on one coin at about 1,000: cut from 6 mm cast sheet (125 mm of cut, about 12 s), the globe engraved into the back face, mirrored (about 20 s), and the words into the front (about 10 s), each face run in a jig from the sheet's own skeleton
a CNC shop The edge on one coin at about 1,000: both arrises rounded 1.5 with a roundover cutter and 100 reeds milled across it, in a vacuum fixture of 24 (about 40 s a coin)

the CNC shop, or a tumbling finisher Polishing one coin's edge: vibratory tumbling in plastic media with an acrylic polishing compound (a batch of 500 overnight), or vapour polishing; the faces are the sheet's own cast faces, masked through the laser work
The set's box: a slide-lid box of 3 mm Smoke cast acrylic, 190 x 40 x 52 outside, with a felt-lined insert of eight 41 mm slots, so the coins stand on edge in spectrum order
